content: The brave man fares better than the timid whenever a sword must be drawn.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Hvötum er betra (Fáfnismál, Stanza 6) — Poetic Edda
explanation: In moments of crisis, fear paralyses hands and clouds perception. Both the brave and the cowardly must face the dangers ordained by life, but the courageous person commits fully to the encounter, making decisive moves that often turn the tide of fortune.
practicalInsight: Face that difficult confrontation or looming task with wholehearted commitment today. Hesitation guarantees defeat.
reflectionPrompt: Where has fear caused you to drag your feet, multiplying the very danger you sought to avoid?
